svg.title: For analytic functions, ray bounds f(tx) = O(tu) imply vanishing jets below u: a first nonzero homogeneous polynomial would be nonzero on a real diagonal by polarization. Conversely bounded order-u derivatives give uniform Taylor bounds. Ray constants may vary; final derivative constants are common. For qa(k) = eika −1, the difference from ika is second order. Product expansion therefore makes P a qa(−k)qa(k) −|k|2 vanish to order three, proving the ghost cancellation. The actual vector matrix is Avec = d∗ 1M(k)d1 + d0d∗ 0, with M(0) = I.
